ELI5: How can I deal with social situations where I cannot relate to anything?

Ask questions about whatever topic. People like to talk. People will continue to talk about their interests for a decent amount of time. You will probably learn a few things about that topic and can then use that information the next time it comes up.

Sometimes this isn't a good strategy. If you're in a group, that can be problematic. If 5 people are talking about an episode of Game of Thrones, and you have never seen the show, just sit and nod. Maybe not literally, but sometimes in a small group, you'll have to sit out of a conversation every now and again.

I find there are a few things everyone can relate to:

  1. growing up--talking about things you did as a kid and then asking them if they did anything crazy/interesting/hobbies/etc. everyone usually has at least one thing they like talking about as a kid (playing vid games, cartoons, music, hanging out with friends, etc.).

  2. sports--i'm assuming this is a guy to guy conversation. even people who don't like sports still know who the local team is. so just making small talk about new players, scores, and the like won't be the most fulfilling conversation but it will pass the time.

  3. family--everyone has parents (except orphans, do NOT talk about family there) and most have siblings. Ask them about their family and talk about yours. a funny story about ur crazy uncle or lucky brother will make people more comfortable sharing things back with you.

Hope this helps! And remember, we're all just people who each have our own stories to tell. You just have to ask =)

People who don't like sports do not necessarily know who the local team is - and nor do they necessarily care. Generalizing sports as something every guy can relate to is a losing proposition. Definitely find out of they are game before pursuing this course - otherwise, it can become uncomfortable, and preferably avoided, quickly.

Bring up something interesting you read about on Voat or on another site. Preferably something not controversial but that other people will have some frame of reference for. For example you could talk about the new images of Pluto.

If someone is giving you a short answer that you can't do much with, narrow the questions.

Do you have any pets?

yeah

Right there might cause you to move on to "do you like movies" and it moves the conversation into an awkward interrogation. Don't move on until you can add to the conversation.

Do you have any pets?

Yeah.

What kind and how many?

Just two cats.

That is cool. How long have you had them for?

Maybe a year or so.

Are they siblings?

Yeah.

I have had pets as siblings before and noticed that siblings play together more than pets that aren't related. Did you notice this too?

No.

So you have only had two cats your entire life?

Well, no. I had some animals growing up but I never noticed their interaction with each other.

Oh okay, I get it. What kind of animals did you have growing up?

I purposely made the conversation as dull as possible and one oft he characters was extremely unresponsive because I have come across people that are like that. A conversation about pets turned led to a conversation about childhood pets which can then segue into childhood interests. Ask questions but don't interrogate the person. Build off off their previous answers and share a little about yourself. It can be as simple as "that happened to me too".

You don't have to like or be interested in the conversation topic initially. Just ask questions and get them to explain stuff to you. It is extremely important for you to be aware of how they are viewing you. If you look disinterested, they won't share as much. If you ask for advice on the best headphones to buy, write down their answer. Even if you aren't going to buy them, it makes you look interested. Eventually you will land on a topic you both are interested in.

The United States is a very introspective country, when given the chance. We generally feel bad that our nation had slavery, that our nation locked up Japanese without due process, that our nation had widespread sex discrimination up until the late 1970s-mid 1980s. We feel bad when we attack the wrong country (Iraq, for example) and we slap ourselves on the forehead over a litany of things that the nation has done wrong. For example, there are white people around today who feel guilt over slavery. But none of these white people ever enslaved anyone. It was their great-great-grandparents, or in some cases it wasn't even them. There are people whose ancestors never held slaves at all, and they still feel guilty. We have buildings that were built by slave efforts, we have massive agricultural industries that arose from slavery and these subsequent industries supply us with extremely affordable food today. White people who had nothing to do with enslavement feel bad about slavery in particular - and that is kind of strange, because modern black people also profit from past slavery to an extent (because the whole nation profits from these past misdeeds).

This guilty feeling brewing under the surface of much of America was brought to a head in the1960s. Around that time, some black people said they wanted to be called "Negroes" instead of "Colored". But soon thereafter they decided that "Negro" was also bad, and so it should be "Afro-American" .. then "African-American" .. then "Black" .. and on and on. Now you had these white people all jumpy and terrified of saying the wrong thing. I'm a physician (who is an independent contractor, so you could say I own my own business even though I work in a hospital.) I have to abide by a metric fuckton of rules on the state and national level to be able to keep my license to practice medicine. One is the federal level the EMTALA law says that I have to provide a medical screening exam and appropriate treatment for medical stabilization to anyone who requests care at the ER when I am on duty. If I violate EMTALA in addition to hefty fines ($50k+) my state medical license is placed in jeopardy because it is also considered patient abandonment because I have a civil and ethical duty to treat. In addition if in providing that care I stray enough from acceptable medical practice my license is also in jeopardy and I could also get sued for millions of dollars.

I may own my business, but if I want to keep practicing medicine, I have to abide by a number of laws and regulations as well as good standards of medical care. If I don't want to abide by those, then I don't deserve a license. Similarly, a pharmacy (and the pharmacists who work there) are also required to abide by a number of laws and regulations. If they don't want to abide by them, they need to find a different business to be in.

If everyone was able to disregard laws they didn't like, you would have chaos and in the field of medicine you would significantly endanger many lives.
